clue.text: Pretended to keep time, given a prod

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: pretended means simulated, faked

explanation.surface: Someone faked keeping the beat until they got a nudge.
explanation.definitionFit: To be prodded is to be roused or spurred into action, which is to be stirred up.

clue.text: Meet regular members of sestet during walk

indicators.note: during means the first piece sits within the period of the second, so it goes inside

parts.note: to amble is to walk slowly

indicators.note: regular members are every other letter, taking the first, third and fifth of the word

explanation.surface: Members of a six-piece ensemble gather while out for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of 'sestet' are S, S, E, which go inside AMBLE after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet as a group is to gather or come together in one place.

clue.text: Ray preserves rare Hindu incantation

indicators.note: preserves means keeps within, so the second piece is held inside the first

parts.note: a manta is a large species of ray, the flat fish

explanation.surface: A fish somehow keeps alive an uncommon Hindu chant.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred word or phrase repeated in Hindu meditation and prayer is exactly this chant.

clue.text: Queen performed overture to opera

parts.note: performed means did, carried out

indicators.note: an overture opens a work, so this takes the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A queen sang the opening of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido, Queen of Carthage, is the heroine of Purcell's opera Dido and Aeneas, which fits the musical theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary founder and ruler of Carthage was a queen, loved and left by Aeneas.

clue.text: 10 perhaps more certain to come across fellow boarder

parts.note: the answer to 10 across names instruments of the wind family, so they are an example of wind

indicators.note: to come across something is to span it, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: more certain means surer

explanation.surface: Woodwinds being surer to come across a fellow lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boarder' suggests a lodger, but here it means someone who rides a board.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rides a sailboard over the water is a kind of boarder.

clue.text: Sweet old man follows the money, as stated

indicators.note: as stated means as spoken, so the letters come from how the words sound

parts.note: lolly is British slang for money, and pop is an old man or father; pop placed after lolly says the sweet's name

explanation.surface: A treat for Dad, who follows the cash, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: LOLLY is British slang for money; POP, a father, comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiled sugar treat on a stick is a classic sweet, the British word for a candy.

clue.text: Maiden interrupts county cricketer's fight

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so this letter goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A maiden over breaks up a county player's struggle at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden is an over in cricket where no runs are scored; a bat is a batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is armed struggle or fighting, as a noun meaning a battle.

clue.text: River goddess lives around South Island

indicators.note: around means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: lives means is, exists

explanation.surface: A water deity dwells around a southern island.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is both the Thames at Oxford and the Egyptian goddess, so the two words fit one answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thames is so called where it flows through Oxford, and the same name belongs to the Egyptian mother deity.

clue.text: He conducted opera in backward province

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera

indicators.note: backward means the word in is read from right to left

parts.note: NI, Northern Ireland, is often called the Province

explanation.surface: A conductor led an opera in a remote region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' reads as describing the province, but it turns the word before it round; Northern Ireland is known in the UK as the Province.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was the famous Italian maestro who conducted Tosca and much else.

clue.text: Old blowers regularly play these

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, the first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: Elderly wind players routinely perform on these instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of 'blowers' are B, O, E, S; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Double-reed woodwind instruments are blown, and players perform on them regularly.

clue.text: Contribution from Vanessa-Mae's troubling conductor

indicators.note: Contribution from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A violinist's input bothers the person leading the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: Vanessa-Mae is a well-known pop-classical violinist, which keeps the surface on music.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminent musician who directs an orchestra is honoured with this Italian title for master.

clue.text: French composer considers cutting speed

indicators.note: cutting means removing, so the second word is taken out of the first

parts.note: considers means deliberates, thinks over
speed means rate, pace

explanation.surface: A French composer weighs up reducing the tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: Léo Delibes wrote the ballets Coppélia and Sylvia and the opera Lakmé in France.

clue.text: Left Gershwin tackling British scales

indicators.note: tackling means taking hold of, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: Ira Gershwin was the lyricist brother of George

explanation.surface: Gershwin leaves to take on British musical scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scales' suggests musical scales but means the zodiac sign of the balance.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh sign of the zodiac is represented by a pair of balances, or scales.

clue.text: Member of top brass better with French first lady

parts.note: to better is to trump, outdo
et is French for and, with
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the first lady of the land

explanation.surface: A senior officer outdone by a French First Lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top brass' means senior officers but here means the leading brass instrument section.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the leading high brass instrument is a member of the brass section.

clue.text: Suite probed by mariners and pioneers

definitions.meaning: a suite is an orchestral work in several movements, here Holst's
the Mariner and Pioneer spacecraft were probes that explored the solar system's worlds

explanation.surface: An orchestral work explored by sailors and trailblazers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mariners and pioneers' read as sailors and settlers, but they are NASA space probes.
explanation.definitionFit: Holst's orchestral suite takes its seven movements from the worlds circling the Sun, which space probes visited.

clue.text: Elgar fiddled with dress, whatever the conditions

indicators.note: fiddled with means tampered with, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The composer Elgar tinkered with a gown in any circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddled' hints at Elgar playing violin, but signals the letters of ELGAR DRESS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Regardless means anyway, in spite of whatever circumstances may apply.

clue.text: I prefer tonight's controversial ballet

indicators.note: controversial means disputed, so the letters are argued into a different order

explanation.surface: A fan picks this evening's contentious dance performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'controversial' is apt: the 1913 premiere of Stravinsky's ballet caused a riot in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Stravinsky's 1913 work for the Ballets Russes is a famous dance piece.

clue.text: Girl meets hunk, ditching second guy from Cork?

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name

indicators.note: ditching second means dropping the second letter of the word for the hunk

parts.note: a he-man is a muscular hunk

explanation.surface: A girl dates a muscleman, dumping her second fellow from Cork.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork is a city and county in Ireland; the question mark flags it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from Cork, in the Republic, is one example of a male native of that country.

clue.text: Mean to welcome ambassador eventually

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: to mean is to intend
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Planning to greet the envoy in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: HE stands for His Excellency, how an ambassador is addressed.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means finally, after everything, at last.

clue.text: Comedienne Phyllis beset first person with retorts

indicators.note: beset means surrounded, so the comedienne's name encloses the other piece

parts.note: Phyllis Diller was an American comedienne
first is abbreviated 1st, written here with I for the figure one

explanation.surface: A comedienne ringed by the first person to answer back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retorts' suggests witty comebacks, fitting a comic, but means glass vessels used to distil.
explanation.definitionFit: A retort is a long-necked vessel used for distilling, so its user makes spirits.

clue.text: Operas in German too much for vocalist

indicators.note: the words are more than the answer needs, which sits inside them across the word gaps

explanation.surface: German-language opera is overwhelming for a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'operaS IN GERman'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vocalist is someone who uses their voice to perform songs.

clue.text: Instrumentalist picks this big name to tour India

indicators.note: to tour is to go around, so the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: a big name is a star, a celebrity
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A musician chooses a celebrity to travel around India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picks' looks like 'chooses' but means plucks strings.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-necked Indian lute is plucked, so a player picks its strings.

clue.text: Writer's copy found in Home Counties

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the copy goes inside the region

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, SE
to crib is to copy

explanation.surface: An author's plagiarism is discovered in the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in South East England.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe was a copyist who wrote out documents by hand.

clue.text: Crew occasionally hush popular violinist

parts.note: a crew is a group of men

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only some letters, here the second and fourth

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

explanation.surface: Sailors now and then silence a well-liked fiddler.
explanation.walkthrough: The alternate letters of 'hush' give U and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Yehudi Menuhin was a celebrated American-born virtuoso of the violin.

clue.text: Low note creates atmosphere

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: A deep musical note sets the tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective for the note but is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: The mood of a place or event is its atmosphere or feeling.

clue.text: Composer's place full of filthy lucre

indicators.note: full of means containing, so the place wraps round the other letters
filthy means dirty, so the letters of lucre are messed up

explanation.surface: A musician's home is packed with dirty money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filthy lucre' is a set phrase for money, but 'filthy' mixes LUCRE into URCEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Purcell was the leading English composer of the Baroque era.

clue.text: Play back-to-front concert

indicators.note: back-to-front means the last letter of the word for play is moved to the front

parts.note: to romp is to play boisterously

explanation.surface: A drama performed in reverse order of a musical event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to-front' moves the last letter P of ROMP to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The Proms are the BBC's summer series of promenade concerts in London.

clue.text: Norma maybe rejects section of a report

indicators.note: rejects means turns back, so the hidden letters are read in reverse
section of means a run of letters is taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: Norma maybe turns down part of a written account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norma' looks like a woman's name but is Bellini's opera; 'section of' takes AREPO from 'a report' and 'rejects' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellini's Norma is one example of a staged musical drama.

clue.text: Briefly try old doctor, one with special instruments

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: try is taken as written
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Quickly test an old doctor, someone with unusual tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Slide brass instruments are among the members of an orchestra's brass section.
